page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs based on the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance features 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There are no local storage drives bundled with this instance, and it does not include any integrated GPUs. Additionally, it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dedicated CPU allocation ensures that the 64 arm64 cores operate without resource contention from other tenants. Because the instance lacks local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators, workloads requiring high-speed local caching or GPU-driven parallel processing must rely on network-attached storage or alternative instance types. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture typically offers a favorable resource density and lower power profile compared to traditional x86 architectures, making this hardware class suitable for scaling multi-threaded workloads that benefit from a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.

This instance configuration is designed for multi-threaded applications, web serving, containerized microservices, and general-purpose enterprise workloads. The 64 dedicated cores and 256.0 GB of memory support concurrent processing tasks, such as application servers, software compilation, and distributed data processing, where local high-speed storage or specialized GPU acceleration is not required.
